children: Shares of Sambhv Steel Tubes Ltd jumped more than 8 percent on Monday, extending their sharp rally from the previous session to 24 percent in two days. Trading volumes surged to several times their recent average amid investor attention on the steelmaker's expansion plans and proposed Rs 100-crore fundraise.

The stock climbed 8.3 percent to Rs 159.8 in morning trade on September 21, after surging 14 percent on Friday. Sambhv Steel Tubes was also among the most actively traded stocks on both the NSE and BSE.

More than 2.8 crore shares had changed hands on the NSE by around 10:15 am, compared with the stock's 20-day average volume of about 28 lakh shares. The stock has gained about 66 percent so far in 2026, compared with a 10.7 percent decline in the Nifty 50.

The latest rally comes after Sambhv Steel Tubes last week issued clarifications related to its proposed preferential issue of 86.95 lakh fully convertible equity warrants at Rs 115 apiece, which would raise about Rs 100 crore.

The company said the issue price remains unchanged at Rs 115 per warrant. It also clarified that the allotment would neither result in a change in control nor exceed 5 percent of the post-issue fully diluted share capital. Management had earlier said the promoter family and management would participate in the warrant issue, with the proceeds intended partly for capacity expansion and working-capital requirements and partly for investment in its wholly owned subsidiary.

The fundraise forms part of a much larger expansion programme at Sambhv Steel Tubes. The company plans to increase its total finished-product capacity from 0.68 million tonnes per annum to more than 2 million tonnes by 2030. Its brownfield expansion of stainless-steel CR coil capacity at Kuthrel has already doubled capacity from 58,000 tonnes to 116,000 tonnes annually, while its Kesda greenfield project and Kuthrel Unit 2 expansion are targeted for commissioning in Q4 FY27.

For the first phase of the Kesda project, Sambhv is adding 360,000 tonnes of capacity. Management said in its August earnings call that it remained confident of beginning trial runs and production in Q4 FY27. The company expects its stainless-steel coil capacity to rise to 476,000 tonnes per annum following the expansion.

However, the growth programme will involve substantial capital expenditure and higher borrowings. Management expects term debt to reach around Rs 800-850 crore and working-capital debt Rs 200-300 crore by the end of FY27. Its current cost of debt is around 7.5-8 percent.

Operationally, Sambhv Steel Tubes reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and net profit in Q1 FY27. Revenue stood at Rs 732 crore, EBITDA at Rs 100 crore and net profit at Rs 56 crore. Sales volumes rose 16 percent year-on-year, while volumes of value-added products increased 27 percent.

For FY27, management has guided for revenue growth of 10-15 percent and EBITDA of Rs 7,500-8,500 per tonne. It expects value-added product sales of around 4 lakh tonnes during the year, including 2.3-2.4 lakh tonnes of MS pipes and tubes, around 90,000 tonnes of GP pipes and coils and about 60,000 tonnes of stainless-steel CR coils.

Management has nevertheless flagged some near-term moderation. It expects softer prices and slower demand during Q2, while stainless-steel margins could also face pressure as import competition increases.
